facts.value: AA pages state MS TOEFL 90 / IELTS 7 and PhD TOEFL 100 / IELTS 7. Those TOEFL cutoffs use the prior scale while Stanford has introduced a new TOEFL score scale for tests from Jan 21, 2026. The department page also lists exemptions for US citizen/permanent resident, English first language, English-taught postsecondary degree, or two consecutive years of English-medium experience in the last 10 years.
conditions: Ask the department to confirm 2027 TOEFL thresholds on the new scale before assessment.

facts.value: Full-time Aero/Astro MS has one Autumn 2027-28 cycle with a final December 1, 2026 deadline. A bachelor’s degree and strong technical preparation in engineering, physics, or comparable science are expected; the specific major is not fixed. Submit the online application, USD 125 fee, two-page single-spaced purpose statement, three recommendations (one academic required; two preferred), scanned transcripts, and English score if applicable. No late applications.
conditions: Applications are reviewed holistically; monitor the application checklist.
exceptions: Previously earned AA or closely related MS holders are not eligible for this external MS.

facts.value: GRE is not required and not considered. The department says MS students are typically self-funded; assistantships may be possible and outside fellowships/loans are potential options. Federal student loans require U.S. citizenship or permanent residence.
conditions: Funding options are not an award guarantee.

facts.value: Aero/Astro PhD has one final Autumn 2027-28 deadline: December 1, 2026. Applicants may apply with a bachelor’s degree; a prior MS is not required. Current Stanford AA MS students who want to add a PhD must finish department paperwork before conferring the MS. PhD entrants without a related MS must add the AA MS internally by petition and approved program proposal at/before beginning year three.
conditions: The internal MS is a PhD progress requirement, not an external admission target.
exceptions: Current AA MS to PhD requires paperwork before MS conferral.

facts.value: PhD application requires online form, USD 125 fee, two-page single-spaced research purpose statement, three references (one academic required, two preferred), transcripts, and English test if applicable. Students in good standing receive support through thesis submission, at least equivalent to a 20-hour RA salary plus tuition for required enrollment; support sources include fellowship, RA, training grants or TA, with Cardinal Care insurance described by the department.
conditions: Summer enrollment requirements vary by department.
exceptions: Department TOEFL cutoff requires confirmation on revised scale.

facts.value: The nonrefundable non-professional graduate application fee is USD 125, due at submission. Eligible applicants may request GRE fee-reduction, program-participation, or school-based waivers before applying; submit at least 10 business days before the program deadline for timely review.
conditions: After payment and submission, the fee is not refundable, including after withdrawal.
exceptions: Waiver eligibility and any limited school-based allotment depend on program/school; late requests are not guaranteed reviewed by the deadline.

facts.value: Standard application requires three academic or professional references, a statement of purpose, experience information and program-tailored supplemental responses. CV/resume, writing samples and other materials vary by program.
conditions: Program-specific page and current directory control each option's supplemental requirements.

facts.value: CEE maintains merit-based financial aid through teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and/or fellowships. Applicants interested in merit-based aid are asked to indicate that interest in the graduate application.
conditions: This describes an application interest signal and possible aid types, not a guaranteed award. Amounts, eligibility and deadlines remain program-specific.

facts.value: Chemical Engineering does not require GRE scores and will not accept them; it publishes no minimum GPA and no required prior field of study or other graduate degree. The department does not accept recommendation letters through Interfolio.
conditions: The 2027-28 external directory lists GRE as not considered for both degrees; applicants still need to meet university English policy and submit department-required materials.

facts.value: Engineering coterm applicants must be current Stanford undergraduates with at least six non-summer quarters and 120 units toward graduation, including applicable AP/transfer units. Admission and offer acceptance must be completed at least one quarter before bachelor's conferral. Department deadlines and criteria vary.
conditions: Engineering standard coterm application requires a statement of purpose, a preliminary program proposal, and Stanford-professor recommendations; some departments require GRE or other material.
exceptions: These Engineering eligibility details do not establish eligibility or terms for Doerr coterm options.

facts.value: CS coterm is only for current, registered Stanford undergraduates and requires at least 120 units toward graduation; students on leave are ineligible. Apply no later than the quarter before expected BS completion. Submit Registrar forms, statement of purpose, resume, unofficial transcripts and three recommendation letters; at least two academic and one CS-faculty recommender are recommended. There is no minimum GPA; 3.5 is recommended for non-CS majors, who are also advised to complete four CS core courses or a mix of core/graduate courses. CS limits applicants to three coterm attempts. The 2026-27/2027-28 deadlines are Winter Oct 6 2026, Spring Jan 8 2027, Autumn Apr 30 2027. A USD 125 fee is assessed only if admitted and accepting. No deferral is allowed; late letters can miss committee review and submitted applications cannot be edited.
conditions: Recommended preparation and GPA are recommendations rather than minimums. Coterm funding is limited; course assistantship may be available after graduate-tuition status.
exceptions: Coterm fee is charged only after acceptance of admission offer; this is different from the nonrefundable external graduate application fee.

facts.value: CS MS applicants need a qualifying bachelor’s degree but need not major in CS; the department recommends strong quantitative/analytical preparation and directs applicants to review its CS Foundation requirements. The MS can be coursework-only or include research. HCP is a part-time MS route for full-time employed people; HCP applicants must reside in the U.S., and international HCP applicants must be employed and located in the U.S. A CS MS is not a guaranteed path to the CS PhD.
conditions: Specific undergraduate coursework is recommended, not a mandatory admission prerequisite in the cited department page. HCP and full-time external routes remain distinct.
exceptions: HCP location/employment restriction applies to HCP route, not full-time MS applicants.

facts.value: CS says GRE is not required and is not considered for MS applicants. Its FAQ says TOEFL is required for applicants whose first language is not English regardless of citizenship, with stated exceptions for U.S. citizens/permanent residents, English first language, or an English-instruction degree. The central Graduate Admissions page also recognizes two years of consecutive full-time English-medium professional/educational experience as an exemption; CS MS FAQ does not mention that exemption.
conditions: Do not silently replace either source rule; ask CS admissions whether the central experience exemption applies to CS MS applicants.

facts.value: Applicants need a qualifying bachelor’s degree; a CS major is not required, but strong quantitative and analytical skills are important. The PhD is research-oriented, with few course requirements and typical completion in 5–6 years. CS does not require or consider GRE scores. The SOP limit is 8,000 characters including spaces; three references and application checklist items are required. Applicants must choose CS MS or PhD and cannot apply to both in the same admissions cycle.
conditions: Current Stanford graduate and undergraduate applicants use the online graduate application for PhD admission; this is not the coterm route.
exceptions: No CS undergraduate major prerequisite is stated.

facts.value: CS states all PhD students are guaranteed funding while they make satisfactory academic progress. External support must be disclosed and may adjust Stanford’s award. A 50% research assistantship covers 8–10 units of tuition and pays salary; lower 10–40% appointments or other funding combinations provide less tuition allowance/salary. RA availability depends on a faculty member, and students must be registered, in good standing, and satisfy payroll requirements.
conditions: The guarantee is conditioned on satisfactory academic progress; exact stipend and tuition arrangement depends on appointment/fellowship and funding source.
exceptions: External awards can change the Stanford funding package; conflicting funding restrictions can limit stacking.

facts.value: Doerr states full financial support for PhD candidates through fellowships, teaching assistantships and research assistantships. Master's students may be eligible for teaching or research assistantships. This is general school guidance, not an individual award or guaranteed package.
conditions: Specific coverage, duration, amount, summer support, continuation rules, and exceptions must be checked by program.
exceptions: Environmental Social Sciences Bulletin specifies five academic years for students in good standing; support after year five is not guaranteed.

facts.value: EE coterm application periods: Winter 2026-27 Sep 15–Oct 26 2026; Spring 2026-27 Dec 3 2026–Jan 13 2027; Autumn 2027-28 Feb 3–Mar 31 2027. Review follows each deadline; decisions may take up to four weeks. Applicants may apply after 120 units, no later than the quarter before expected undergraduate completion, and need at least one quarter of overlap. GRE is not required.
conditions: Coterm course transfer/eligibility rules are department and Registrar scoped.

facts.value: EE MS is a terminal coursework-based program with 45 units, no thesis, and a typical full-time completion time of 1.5–2 years. It has autumn entry only; deadline for Autumn 2027-28 is Dec 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific and offer response is due Apr 15, 2027. Later PhD study requires applying through the separate PhD process.
conditions: The full-time MS route is separate from coterm and current doctoral-student added-MS options.

facts.value: EE PhD has autumn-only admission; Autumn 2027-28 deadline is Dec 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific, with decisions in late February and offer response due Apr 15, 2027. An MS is not required; typical completion is 5–7 years. Students in good standing receive full support for the PhD duration: year-one fellowship, usually advisor RA thereafter, full-time tuition, living stipend/salary and 50% Cardinal Care premium subsidy. Conditions include advisor/funding arrangement, 8–10 units during academic quarters, GPA at least 3.0 and timely progress. External tuition-plus-stipend awards typically replace the first fellowship.
conditions: Later assistantship continuation depends on satisfactory progress and faculty funding.
exceptions: External funding can replace or adjust Stanford support.

facts.value: EE does not require GRE. The department requests unofficial transcripts from every attended college, a purpose statement up to two single-spaced pages, three recommendations, and a USD 125 application fee. TOEFL/IELTS is required unless a central Graduate Admissions waiver applies; EE gives TOEFL 90 / IELTS 7 for admission consideration and TOEFL 109 / IELTS 8 to avoid the placement test. Applicants may request both the SoE and department application fee waivers, but only one is granted; EE preference is low-income or first-generation U.S. citizens/permanent residents.
conditions: EE states central office decides all English waivers; confirm TOEFL score scale for 2027 applicants.
exceptions: Late official transcripts/test scores may be processed if unofficial copies were on time; late recommendation letters may miss committee review.

facts.value: School of Engineering departments award graduate fellowships, research assistantships, and teaching assistantships. The Bulletin does not establish a schoolwide funding amount, guarantee, eligibility, or deadline.
conditions: Specific award access, amount, coverage, duration, renewal, and cycle deadline must be checked for the selected program.

facts.value: For 2027-28 entry, if no exemption applies, official TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic is required. Minimum consideration scores: TOEFL 90 before Jan 21 2026 or 4.5 on/after that date; IELTS Academic 7. Score validity is two years. Individual programs may require higher scores.
conditions: University exemption applies if applicant is a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, first-language English speaker, has a qualifying English-instruction postsecondary degree, or has at least two consecutive years of full-time English-medium professional/educational experience in the past 10 years.
exceptions: Scores below the higher placement-exemption threshold require the English Placement Test before enrollment; no exception is stated.

facts.value: Environmental Social Sciences PhD admits for fall only. For the 2027-28 cycle, the application deadline is November 17, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific; applicants must choose the Environmental Behavioral Sciences (EBS) or Global Environmental Policy (GEP) subplan, and late applications are not accepted.
conditions: The Knight-Hennessy application is separate and has its own October 6, 2026 deadline.

facts.value: Geophysics admits to the department rather than an individual advisor or research group. The committee weighs academic achievement, recommendations, statement of purpose, research fit and potential, and work/life experience holistically; it states no minimum GPA. Applicants are encouraged to contact faculty about research fit and upcoming advising capacity. Applicants pursuing the Geophysics MS as a first step toward a PhD are asked to contact potential faculty advisors; applicants with a BS or MS may apply to the PhD.
conditions: The page displayed a 2025-26 date; that date is not used as a 2027-28 deadline. Current 2027-28 deadline and GRE remain sourced from the live directory.

facts.value: Applicants may apply to one Stanford graduate degree program per academic year; the sole stated exception is applying to two Biosciences PhD programs in one application.
conditions: Do not apply this portal rule to coterm, professional-school, or internal add-degree processes without route-specific support.

facts.value: For non-professional graduate admission, applicants must hold or expect before enrollment a U.S. bachelor's degree or recognized international equivalent. Citizens and residents of all countries are eligible; a department may impose additional preparation and selection rules.
conditions: Applicants with non-U.S. credentials may be required to submit a WES evaluation after accepting an offer; it is not required at application.

facts.value: GRE General and Subject test requirements are set program by program as required, optional, or not considered. For 2027-28, the university's earliest valid test date is Sept 1 2021; a program may use a stricter period.
conditions: A program that does not consider GRE will not show GRE scores to its admissions committee.

facts.value: Materials Science and Engineering lists fellowships, assistantships, and loans as graduate funding options. This does not specify a particular award, amount, coverage, eligibility, duration, renewal rule, or deadline.
conditions: Review specific MSE funding pages and individual award rules before stating eligibility or coverage.
Dates are exact entry-term deadlines; HCP dates are separate from full-time. Full-time rows absent here are not assigned a value.
exceptions: BIOE and CEE entries were not present in the captured current directory even though Bulletin inventory metadata says externally admissible; confirm through current department pages.

facts.value: CEE accepts fall graduate applications once annually through Stanford Graduate Admissions. Required materials are uploaded academic records from every college/university attended for at least a year or current degree enrollment, statement of purpose (maximum three single-spaced pages, two recommended), three recommendations, resume/CV, and TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic if no exemption applies. Official transcripts are requested only after an admitted applicant accepts. GRE is not considered; Interfolio recommendations and emailed materials are not accepted. Applicants with related non-CEE backgrounds may apply but may need extra preparatory study after admission.
conditions: PhD purpose statement should address research area and potentially relevant faculty.
English exemptions use the central Graduate Admissions policy.
exceptions: A traditional civil engineering undergraduate major is not mandatory.
Applications cannot be changed after submission.

facts.value: For Autumn 2027 entry, CEE MS, Engineer and PhD applications and supporting materials are due December 1, 2026 at 11:59 pm Pacific Standard Time; the same date applies to coterm MS. Fee waiver requests should be made by November 17, 2026, ten business days before the deadline. Decisions are released February-April 2027; admitted applicants must reply by April 15, 2027. Admitted MS students can request a one-time deferral to the next autumn by June 30, 2027; PhD and Engineer admits cannot use this deferral.
conditions: Department page labels the 2027 deadline PST; preserve its published timezone.

facts.value: CEE FAQ still states old-scale TOEFL 90 for School of Engineering MS applicants, while central Graduate Admissions publishes the revised TOEFL scale for tests on/after January 21, 2026. The current application page defers to central TOEFL iBT/IELTS Academic rules and exemptions. Do not apply the FAQ score to a new-scale 2027 applicant without resolution.
conditions: Resolve TOEFL score-scale discrepancy with CEE/Graduate Admissions before automated assessment.

facts.value: CEE MS is a coursework-based degree with core courses, technical electives, seminars and unrestricted electives; thesis and research are not required. It can be finished in three quarters, though most students take four or five. CEE aims to support MS students where possible, usually describing any award in the admission letter. RA positions for MS are rare and usually in the second study year; course assistantships are competitive and generally favor continuing students. Neither is guaranteed.
conditions: Individual MS specializations have separate program plans.
No assistantship or fellowship amount should be inferred.

facts.value: CEE PhD combines coursework and research, requires service as teaching assistant for one course, and averages five to six years. Engineering PhD students in good standing receive support through thesis submission at least equivalent to a 20-hour RA salary plus tuition for required enrollment and Cardinal Care insurance. Support may come from fellowship, RA, training grant or TA; the department/advisor arranges it and cannot require external funding or self-funding as a condition of entry or continuation. Entering PhD applicants are considered for Engineering/Doerr fellowships with the admission application; Stanford Graduate Fellowships are selectively nominated and offer 12 quarters of stipend plus tuition for 8-10 units.
conditions: Summer enrollment requirements vary by department.

facts.value: CEE Engineer degree is a post-master's professional research route requiring a thesis and approximately one to two further full-time years after the MS. The current external graduate directory explicitly lists CEE Engineer alongside MS/PhD for Autumn 2027 admission, with December 1, 2026 deadline and GRE not considered. CEE says any MS/Engineer support would generally appear in the admission letter; no guaranteed Engineer award or renewal schedule is published on the reviewed funding page.
conditions: A prior master's degree is the normal academic preparation.
Do not present potential support as a guaranteed award.

facts.value: MS&E MS applicants need an engineering or related quantitative degree with multivariable differential calculus and linear algebra. The department expects both this mathematical preparation and general programming before beginning graduate study, while its FAQ specifically requires multivariable calculus before applying and permits general programming after admission or during the MS. Additional statistics, economics and programming are preferred, and work experience is not required. The degree develops quantitative decision, strategy and organizational leadership skills; 45 units can be spread over about three to four quarters.

For Autumn 2027 MS&E MS and PhD, the current directory gives December 1, 2026 deadline and GRE General required with Mathematics Subject optional; the MS page specifies 11:59 pm PST. The department FAQ requires online application, at most two-page single-spaced purpose statement, resume, uploaded unofficial transcripts, recommendation letters and required test scores. New external applicants should include at least one academic recommender. Late applications are refused; MS decisions usually come in mid-March and PhD in mid-February via the application status page. Official scores received after deadline can still be attached if unofficial scores were entered on time, but review after two weeks is not guaranteed.
conditions: GRE requirement is specific to MS&E; no work-experience waiver is offered.
The university English-test exemptions and minimums apply where relevant.

facts.value: MS&E PhD students without external funding are guaranteed course assistantship support while making satisfactory progress; first-year doctoral students typically receive fellowships, and later fellowship/RA possibilities exist. MS funding is not guaranteed: students may apply for quarter-by-quarter course or research assistantships, generally confirmed at quarter start. The department says fewer than 10% of its over-200 MS students receive these appointments, mainly returning students. MS applicants should prepare to self-fund if no appointment is awarded; US federal loans are limited to US citizens/permanent residents.
conditions: PhD support continues only with satisfactory degree progress.
MS appointments are one quarter only and must be sought anew.

facts.value: ICME accepts MS and PhD applications for autumn entry through separate selections in Stanford Graduate Admissions; applicants can choose only one of the two in a given year and an unsuccessful PhD application is not reconsidered for MS. Upload unofficial transcripts for institutions attended for at least a full-time year, CV/resume, three recommendations (at least one academic strongly recommended), statements, and the required program supplement. The supplement asks for advanced course preparation with three mathematics classes required for consideration, professional/research experience and a short lay explanation of goals; PhD applicants identify nonbinding research/faculty interests, MS applicants select a track and explain career goals. GRE scores are not accepted or considered. Official transcripts are required after admission acceptance.
exceptions: An academic reference may be replaced by three professional references when the applicant graduated five or more years ago.
An optional fourth recommender may serve as backup; three submitted letters complete the requirement.

facts.value: The 2027-28 directory lists ICME MS full-time and HCP autumn entry with January 29, 2027 deadline; PhD autumn entry is due December 1, 2026. HCP is only for MS, selected within the application, and is considered in the same pool as full-time MS. Full-time MS is designed for two years and cannot be completed wholly online; MS-to-PhD transition requires a new application. ICME says all PhD students in good standing receive departmental-standard funding through a combination of fellowship, RA and TA; MS funding is not guaranteed.
conditions: The 2027 deadlines come from the live program directory, rather than older FAQ examples.
PhD funding depends on good standing.

facts.value: MS Design requires a science/engineering BS or equivalent and at least one year of professional employment at application submission. A BS-equivalent degree requires a supporting letter from a faculty adviser or department representative of the awarding institution. No specific design employment is required, but applicants must demonstrate a usable skill toolkit and design potential through a required digital portfolio URL. The Autumn 2027 application is due December 1, 2026 at 11:59 pm Pacific Time with a two-page maximum purpose statement, three recommendations, unofficial transcripts, applicable English results and portfolio; GRE is not required/considered. Decisions are sent by end of March 2027.
exceptions: Applicants with under one year of professional employment are not considered.
Portfolio has no fixed project-count or format rule.

facts.value: MS Design is a full-time six-quarter, two-academic-year project-based degree, with core design courses, methods/domain focus, and a year-long capstone. It is not in session during summer. The program uses Stanford Graduate Engineering 8-10 unit tuition rate; this page does not itself publish a 2027-28 amount. MS Design students are offered course assistantships upon acceptance to offset attendance cost, but offer terms vary each year. Knight-Hennessy is a separate application with October 6, 2026 1 pm Pacific deadline for the 2027 cohort.
conditions: Do not infer a fixed assistantship amount, duration or renewal rule.
Knight-Hennessy is separately selected and is not automatic admission funding.

facts.value: Bioengineering MS and PhD accept applicants with an eligible bachelor's degree or equivalent without a department minimum GPA, prescribed undergraduate field or prior graduate degree. GRE is not considered. Applicants submit the online form, uploaded unofficial academic records including transcript legends, a statement of purpose of at most three single-spaced pages (two recommended), three recommendations, resume/CV and applicable English result. Official transcripts are requested only after admission is accepted; late materials may not be reviewed.
exceptions: No specific undergraduate major is required.
Older BioE page still labels Fall 2026; current 2027 deadlines come from live directory.

facts.value: The live Graduate Admissions directory lists both Bioengineering MS and PhD for Autumn 2027-28 with December 1, 2026 deadline and GRE General/Subject not considered. Department review is holistic; virtual interviews are by invitation. BioE timeline says PhD decisions usually arrive by early March, MS decisions by early April, and admitted applicants start in September. Deferral requests are considered individually for no more than one year, generally for military, medical, visa or education reasons; this statement was posted with the older Fall 2026 cycle and must be rechecked for a 2027 offer.

The Bioengineering MS combines core quantitative biology/systems courses, technical electives, seminars and unrestricted electives with an individually planned focus and faculty adviser. It is expected to take about one year and has no thesis requirement. Named areas such as biomedical computation and imaging are examples of focus, not separate admission targets.

Bioengineering PhD research and coursework generally take five to six years; first-year students can rotate through three labs before selecting an adviser, and teaching assistant service for two courses is required. Competitive preparation includes strong quantitative mathematics/physical science and biology from coursework or research, but the department states no fixed pre-application course list. Engineering/Medicine fellowships are considered with the PhD application; Stanford Graduate Fellowship requires nomination and can provide a quarterly stipend plus 8-10 unit tuition for 12 quarters. Training-grant availability varies annually and PhD aid notifications are sent in March/April. These are selective opportunities, not guaranteed individual awards.

Chemical Engineering MS is offered externally only through the part-time Honors Cooperative Program, not as a full-time MS. HCP accepts spring and autumn entry; current 2027-28 directory and department page list January 8, 2027 for spring and April 2, 2027 for autumn. The HCP application needs an online form, two-page purpose statement, three recommendations, education/test information and uploaded unofficial transcripts; Interfolio is excluded. GRE is not accepted. Related non-ChemE majors may apply but may need extra background study after admission. The department says it cannot offer financial aid to MS students, and Knight-Hennessy does not cover this part-time route. Decisions follow within about a month after the application deadline.
conditions: The page calls submissions rolling but says final decisions follow completion of the deadline pool.
Full-time MS admission is not offered.

facts.value: Chemical Engineering PhD accepts bachelor-level entrants for Autumn 2027; prior MS and fixed undergraduate major are not required. The December 1, 2026 11:59 pm PST deadline applies to all components including three references. Submit the online application, uploaded unofficial transcripts, purpose statement up to two single-spaced pages, one-page research-experience list in the portal Resume/CV field, recommendations and applicable English scores. GRE is neither required nor accepted. Applicants from varied STEM fields are eligible; the committee values quantitative mathematics/physical-science preparation, biology and relevant ChemE concepts. Faculty do not directly admit applicants to their labs; applications cannot be updated after submission and late recommendations are not reviewed. Decisions usually arrive January/February.
exceptions: The portal describes a three-page CV field, but department specifically limits the research-experience list to one page.
No prior MS or exact course checklist is an eligibility prerequisite.

facts.value: Chemical Engineering PhD students in good standing are funded through thesis submission at least to the School of Engineering standard of 20-hour RA salary, tuition for required registration and Cardinal Care health insurance. Support can be fellowship, RA, training grant or TA and is arranged by the department/adviser; the student cannot be required to self-fund or obtain an external fellowship to enter or continue. The exact individual funding mix can vary by quarter.

Materials Science and Engineering accepts autumn MS and PhD applications through Stanford Graduate Admissions. For 2027 entry, PhD is due December 1, 2026 and MS January 12, 2027; GRE General/Subject are not accepted. Required materials include online application, unofficial transcripts/record legends, CV, purpose statement of no more than three single-spaced pages (two recommended), three signed institutional-letterhead recommendations with contact details, and applicable English test results. Official transcripts are required after accepted offer. PhD decisions usually arrive by late January, MS by early March; admitted students must reply by April 15, 2027. Deferrals up to one year are case-specific, usually military, medical, visa or education-related.

MSE welcomes MS/PhD applicants from engineering, related science and mathematics degrees; a prior materials major is not required. External applicants cannot apply directly to the MSE Engineer degree, which admits internal candidates only. The MS is intended as terminal study; applicants seeking both MS and PhD should apply for PhD, and may request MS consideration in the application if PhD admission is not offered.
exceptions: Internal Engineer is a different selection route from external MS/PhD.
MS reconsideration of a PhD applicant requires the applicant to opt in and remains discretionary.

facts.value: MSE guarantees PhD students in satisfactory degree progress tuition, living stipend/salary and health insurance subsidy for the program duration; external fellowship support is topped up to department standard if insufficient. The department financial-aid page says MS students do not receive fellowships and are rarely RAs, while its FAQ says a limited number of MS fellowships may be awarded after competitive merit review. Treat MS fellowship availability as an official-source conflict, with no guaranteed award; ask MSE admissions which statement governs the 2027 cohort.
conditions: PhD continuation requires satisfactory degree progress.
Resolve the conflicting MS fellowship statements before showing a categorical no-awards rule.

facts.value: Mechanical Engineering MS applicants need a BS in engineering, physics or comparable science; an applicant who has completed or entered a Mechanical Engineering or closely related master's program, or equivalent international degree, is ineligible for the external MSME. The application requires online form, fee, two-page single-spaced purpose statement, MS supplementary responses, CV, three letters (at least one academic, two preferred), unofficial transcripts for institutions attended for at least a year, and applicable English test. GRE is not accepted through January 2027. The Autumn 2027 full-time application is due December 1, 2026; HCP has separate winter/spring windows in the live directory.
exceptions: Already enrolled in a related master's, not only a completed degree, triggers the MS exclusion.
HCP part-time deadlines must not be replaced by the full-time deadline.

facts.value: Mechanical Engineering PhD applicants need a BS in engineering, physics or comparable science and apply via Stanford Graduate Admissions with online form, fee, two-page single-spaced purpose statement, PhD supplement (research/faculty interests and short prompts), CV, three letters (at least one academic), unofficial transcripts and applicable English results. GRE is not accepted through January 2027. Autumn 2027 entry is due December 1, 2026. The department also lists winter 2026-27 and spring 2026-27 deadlines, but applicants must contact mechanical@stanford.edu before starting or submitting those off-cycle applications.

Mechanical Engineering MS is coursework-based with no thesis required; the department offers research credit by faculty arrangement. The PhD is research-intensive. ME selectively awards entering graduate fellowships, typically to PhD students; School/department awards commonly provide 8-10 units of tuition and a quarterly stipend for three to five quarters. RAs typically cover 8-10 units and salary for 20 weekly research hours, while TAs/CAs are mainly for continuing students and a limited number of entrants. These are potential funding arrangements, not an unconditional MS award or a fixed multi-year offer.

Aeronautics and Astronautics Engineer degree is an internal continuation/transfer after an MS. Students submit a Graduate Program Authorization Petition, purpose statement describing thesis topic and a faculty letter confirming preparation and willingness to advise, several weeks before the end of their current degree. This is not a 2027 external application target.

Chemical Engineering Engineer degree applications are open only to active Chemical Engineering MS or PhD candidates; the Bulletin does not establish direct external admission. The reviewed public admissions page gives no separate deadline, documents, funding or renewal terms for this internal request; active students must obtain them from ChemE student services.

Materials Science and Engineering Engineer degree provides graduate training beyond the MSE MS and admits internal candidates only. The department FAQ explicitly instructs external applicants not to put Engineer on the application. Internal deadline/materials were not published on the reviewed public department pages and require direct MSE student-services confirmation.

Mechanical Engineering Engineer degree requires a master's-level foundation, an additional year of study and research thesis. Admission is not granted until a faculty member agrees to supervise the thesis; external master's holders can apply if sufficiently qualified and have arranged thesis supervision and financial aid. Stanford MS students usually arrange continuation during their MS. The degree needs 90 total units, including up to 18 thesis units and at least 21 advanced technical units beyond the MS; a 3.0 GPA in non-thesis work beyond MS is required. Current Graduate Admissions directory does not list ME Engineer as an open 2027 entry; external applicants must confirm application window with ME student services rather than assume the MS/PhD deadline.

The interdisciplinary Engineering MS is for students already admitted to a Stanford School of Engineering graduate program whose proposed area does not fit an existing degree. A proposed advising department reviews the transfer application and recommends it to School of Engineering Student Affairs. Apply before completing 18 units in the proposed program with a statement of objectives, coherent coursework and why existing programs do not fit, usually including a willing faculty adviser. Transfer uses a Graduate Program Authorization Petition, not a direct external Engineering MS admission.
